title: Site-Directed Immobilization of Bone Morphogenetic Protein 2 to Solid Surfaces by Click Chemistry
protocol: Clone human mature BMP2 by site-directed mutagenesis using PCR.
Amplify human mature BMP2 from a p25N-hmBMP2 vector with specific forward and reverse primers.
Introduce an amber stop codon at the position of the first lysine in the mature part of BMP2.
Perform PCR reaction according to specified conditions: denaturation, annealing, elongation, and final extension.
Purify the PCR product using a commercially available kit following manufacturer recommendations.
Digest the PCR product with NdeI at 37 °C for 45 min using specified volumes and buffer conditions.
Heat-inactivate the enzyme after digestion of PCR product with NdeI at 65 °C for 5 min.
Digest the PCR product with BamHI at 37 °C for 1 h using specified volumes and buffer conditions.
Heat-inactivate the enzyme after digestion of PCR product with BamHI at 80 °C for 5 min.
Digest pET11a-pyrtRNA vector with NdeI at 37 °C for 2 h and 45 min using specified volumes and buffer conditions.
Heat-inactivate the enzyme after digestion of pET11a-pyrtRNA vector with NdeI at 65 °C for 5 min.
Digest pET11a-pyrtRNA vector with BamHI at 37 °C for 1 h using specified volumes and buffer conditions.
Heat-inactivate the enzyme after digestion of pET11a-pyrtRNA vector with BamHI at 80 °C for 5 min.
Separate digested vector from undigested vector and digestion remnants by agarose gel electrophoresis (0.8% agarose, 60 min at 100 V).
Ligate the digested BMP2-K3TAG insert with digested pET11a-pyrtRNA backbone at room temperature for 2 h using specified volumes of ligase buffer and DNA ligase.
Perform co-transformation of pET11a-pyrtRNA-BMP2-K3Plk and pSRF-duet-pyrtRNAsynth in BL21(DE3) bacteria.
Add 50 ng of each plasmid to the bacteria.
Place the mixture on ice for 30 min.
Heat shock at 42 °C for 50 s.
Place on ice for 5 min.
Add 500 µL of Lysogeny Broth (LB) medium in the mixture.
Shake at 300 rpm for 60 min.
Spread 100 µL of the bacterial mixture onto pre-warmed kanamycin (50 µg/mL)/ampicillin (100 µg/mL) plates.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Propagate a single colony overnight in 50 mL of LB medium with 50 µg/mL of kanamycin and 100 µg/mL of ampicillin at 37 °C.
Dilute overnight cultures 1:20 into 800 mL of Terrific Broth (TB) medium supplemented with 50 µg/mL of kanamycin and 100 µg/mL of ampicillin.
Grow at 37 °C until an OD600 of 0.7 is reached.
Add propargyl-L-lysine to a final concentration of 10 mM.
Collect a 100 µL sample from the culture before IPTG induction.
Induce gene expression by adding IPTG to a final concentration of 1 mM.
Grow the culture at 37 °C for 16 h in an orbital shaker at 180 rpm.
Collect a 100 µL sample from the culture.
Centrifuge the whole culture at 9000 x g for 30 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the bacterial pellet in 30 mL of TBSE buffer (10 mM Tris, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA) with 1:1000 (v/v) 2-mercaptoethanol (freshly added).
Handle 2-mercaptoethanol under the fume hood.
Weigh an empty centrifuge beaker and transfer the resuspended pellet into it.
Centrifuge at 6,360 x g for 20 min.
Discard the supernatant and weigh the beaker with the pellet.
Subtract the weight of the empty beaker to calculate the weight of the pellet.
Freeze the pellet at -20 °C in the short term or at -80 °C in the long term if pausing.
Thaw the pellet at room temperature upon resuming the protocol.
Resuspend the pellet in STE buffer using 200 mL for every 10 g of pellet.
Sonicate the suspension on ice (10 min with 40 s pulse, 20 s brake, and 30% amplitude).
Centrifuge at 6,360 x g for 20 min.
Discard the supernatant and weigh the pellet.
Repeat the sonication and centrifugation steps four times.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 mL of TBS buffer using 10 mL/g of pellet.
Centrifuge at 6,360 x g for 20 min.
Discard the supernatant and weigh the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in nuclease buffer with freshly added Benzonase using 10 mL/g of pellet.
Incubate the suspension overnight at room temperature on a stirring plate (30 rpm).
Add Triton buffer to the suspension to achieve a 0.5 volume part ratio.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature (no stirring).
Centrifuge at 6,360 x g for 20 min.
Discard the supernatant and weigh the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in TE buffer using 8 mL/g of pellet.
Centrifuge at 6,360 x g for 20 min.
Discard the supernatant and weigh the pellet.
Add 4 mL/g of 25 mM NaAc pH 5.0 to resuspend the pellet.
Add 5 mL/g of 6 M GuCl with 1 mM DTT (freshly added) to the suspension.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C on a stirring plate at 30 rpm.
Centrifuge at 75,500 x g for 20 min.
Collect the supernatant containing unfolded monomeric BMP2 protein.
Concentrate the extract to 20 OD/mL using a 3 kDa molecular weight cut-off membrane in a concentrating cell.
Add concentrated monomers in single drops to Renaturation buffer while stirring at 30 rpm.
Incubate at room temperature for 120 h in the dark.
Adjust the pH of the solution to 3.0 using concentrated HCl.
Dialyze the solution against 1 mM HCl.
Concentrate the dialyzed solution using a 10 kDa molecular weight cut-off membrane in a concentrating cell.
Equilibrate the solution by adding buffer A (20 mM NaAc, 30% isopropanol).
Centrifuge the solution at 4700 x g for 15 min.
Equilibrate the column for ion exchange on a fast protein liquid chromatography system with 150 mL of buffer A.
Load the protein solution onto the equilibrated column.
Elute fractions using a linear gradient of buffer B (20 mM NaAc, 30% isopropanol, 2 M NaCl) using 100 mL of buffer B.
Collect 2 mL fractions.
Analyze 20 µL of each fraction by SDS Polyacrylamide gel (12%) electrophoresis and Coomassie Brilliant Blue staining.
Incubate 20 µM BMP2-WT with different ratios of NaAsc to CuSO4 in H2O on a rotating mixer (20 rpm) overnight at RT.
Adjust the concentration of NaAsc accordingly while keeping CuSO4 constant at 0.5 mM for each ratio tested.
Add loading buffer containing 5% 2-mercaptoethanol to the samples.
Incubate the sample at 95 °C for 6 min.
Analyze reduced and non-reduced samples by SDS-Polyacrylamide gel (12%) electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE).
Stain the Coomassie stained SDS-PAGE gels.
Incubate 20 µM BMP2-K3Plk with different ratios of THPTA to CuSO4.
Use 5 mM NaAsc and 200 µM 3-Azido-7-hydroxycoumarin for the reaction.
Start with 50 µM THPTA and 0.5 mM of CuSO4 in H2O (50 µL total volume).
Perform reactions at different ratios: (7:1); (10:1); (12:1); (15:1); (20:1).
Incubate the reaction for 24 h at RT on a rotating mixer (20 rpm).
Prepare samples in reduced and non-reduced conditions.
Analyze the prepared samples by SDS-PAGE.
Visualize the gels under excitation channel with specific wavelength for 3-Azido-7-hydroxycoumarin (λabs = 404 nm; λem = 477 nm).
Incubate 20 μM of BMP2-K3Plk or BMP2-WT with 20 µL of azide-activated agarose beads in a total volume of 500 µL in reaction buffer for 2 h at RT on a rotating mixer (20 rpm).
Add 5 mM EDTA to stop the reaction.
Incubate the mixture for 15 min at RT on a rotating mixer (20 rpm).
Centrifuge samples at 20,000 x g for 1 min at RT.
Collect the supernatants.
Wash the pellet containing the beads three times with 1,000 µL of HBS500 buffer.
Wash the pellet containing the beads three times with 1,000 µL of 4 M MgCl2.
Wash the pellet containing the beads two times with 1,000 µL of phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Centrifuge at 20,000 x g for 1 min at RT after each washing step and collect supernatants.
Store coupled beads in 1,000 µL of PBS at 4 °C.
Incubate 50 μL of BMP2-K3Plk functionalized beads with 1 µM of Texas Red labeled BMPR-IAEC and 150 µL of HBS500 buffer at RT for 1 h on a rotating mixer (20 rpm).
Centrifuge the beads at 20,000 x g for 1 min at RT.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash the beads with 1000 µL of HBS500 buffer.
Repeat washing step an additional 3 times.
Centrifuge at 20,000 x g for 1 min at RT after each washing step.
Resuspend the beads in 500 µL of PBS.
Pipette 50 µL of resuspended beads onto a glass cover slide.
Set the microscope filter between 561 or 594 nm.
Detect Texas Red–BMPR-IAEC–BMP2-K3Plk functionalized beads using fluorescent microscopy.
Take pictures of the detected beads.
Culture promyoblastic C2C12 cells in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium with 10% Fetal Calf Serum, 100 U/mL penicillin G and 100 µg/mL streptomycin at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere at 5% CO2.
Seed C2C12 cells at a density of 3 × 104 cells/well into a 96-well microplate.
Allow cells to attach overnight.
Remove medium from the wells.

Incubate C2C12 cells with 0.5-200 nM of BMP2-WT or BMP2-K3Plk in 100 µL/well of DMEM (2% FCS, 100 U/mL penicillin G and 100 µg/mL streptomycin) at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere at 5% CO2 for 72 hours.
Remove medium from the wells after incubation.
Wash cells with 100 µL of PBS per well.
Lyse cells at room temperature with 100 µL/well of lysis buffer (1% NP-40, 0.1 M glycine, pH 9.6, 1 mM MgCl2, 1 mM ZnCl2) on a shaking plate for 1 hour.
Add 100 µL/well of ALP buffer (0.1 M glycine, pH 9.6, 1 mM MgCl2, 1 mM ZnCl2) with 1 mg/mL p-nitrophenylphosphate to the cell lysate.
Measure absorption at 405 nm in a multiplate reader after adding the ALP buffer.
Generate dose response curves and EC50 values using a logistic model, y = A2 + (A1-A2)/(1 + (x/x0)p).
Culture promyoblastic C2C12 cells in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium with 10% Fetal Calf Serum, 100 U/mL penicillin G and 100 µg/mL streptomycin at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere at 5% CO2.
Seed C2C12 cells at a density of 3 × 104 cells/well in a 96-well microplate.
Let cells attach overnight.
Remove medium and add 20 µL/well of BMP2-K3Plk coupled beads from a PBS suspension.
Prepare a solution of 0.4% low-melting-point agarose in DMEM.
Melt the agarose in the microwave (600 W for 3 min) and let it cool down in a water bath at 37 °C until use.
Add 20 µL of 0.4% low-melting-point agarose to each well (covering beads and cells).
Centrifuge at 2000 x g for 5 min at 20 °C.
Add 80 µL DMEM with 2% FCS, 100 U/mL penicillin G and 100 µg/mL streptomycin to each well.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere at 5% CO2 for 72 h.
Remove medium carefully without detaching the solidified 0.4% agarose.
Add 100 µL/well of 1-Step NBT/BCIP substrate solution to each well.
Analyze alkaline phosphatase staining using light microscopy immediately after the purple staining becomes apparent.
Use bright field microscopy and take pictures.
